speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what has been the take-up rate for the Off-peak Monthly Travel Pass for persons with disabilities and senior citizens; (b) why was it discontinued without prior notice; and (c) whether there are plans to provide cheaper off-peak or weekend travel options to encourage senior citizens to stay active.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the reason for scrapping the $40 monthly unlimited off-peak travel pass for senior citizens; (b) how many seniors are affected by the scrapping of the pass; and (c) what percentage of seniors have switched to buying the $60 Senior Citizen Monthly Concession Pass.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Regular commuters among this group can also buy the monthly concession pass at half the price of the regular adult monthly pass.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The new scheme was launched with wide publicity.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: PTC, the Land Transport Authority and the public transport operators have placed posters at all Mass Rapid Transit stations and buses since the middle of December last year.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The fact that there was quite a lot of discussion on the ground on this means that it affects these 200 users.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: When the scheme was formulated, I suppose we were optimistic that there would be many who will benefit and make the switch.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Of the handful who probably are adversely affected, how best to do it?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Well, my favourite Member of Parliament (MPs) has good solutions.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Good local MPs can always come up with local solutions.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: When we know a particular resident has been inconvenienced because of this, and yet despite the various 25% discount and so on, still could not afford their transport fares, as a local MP, we do chip in, if I discover such cases.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am quite sure Er Dr Lee will know how to do it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just a question about the experimental effect because it seems like people have switched from the off-peak pass to the all-day pass.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will this increase senior citizens travelling in peak periods and, therefore, actually defeating the purpose of the experiment in the first place?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But we would not know until it starts.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, we will analyse the impact of these various new schemes that have just been brought in.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is just a few weeks in the run and we will see whether we need to refine the scheme as we go along.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Last week, I was reading about the death of the famous founder of IKEA.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He is a legend and there are many stories about him.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I remember his Chief Executive Officer always related an anecdote where, in a board meeting, the founder questioned him, "What are the mistakes you have done?" Meaning that, in life, we must always experiment, try out things.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If you never did, you never tried out anything, then that is your biggest mistake.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Why not give the senior citizens the flexibility of choice between the off-peak pass and the all-day pass?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But now that we have tried this experiment and found that the off-peak pass has failed miserably, why do we want to do it again?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, yes, while I encourage making mistakes, trying out new things, but when we have discovered something does not work and we keep on banging our head against the wall, why do we do that?
